newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico temporarily stops fertilizer exports - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico temporarily stops fertilizer exports - paper.

text.p: Mexico temporarily suspended fertilizer exports because of internal disruptions in supply and demand that have caused internal prices to rise up to 45 percent, daily La Jornada said Tuesday.

Citing Jose Bonilla, the president of the National Confderation of Small Property Owners, La Jornada said the suspension was agreed between state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) and the National Industrial Chemicals Association, known as the ANIQ.
Bonilla told La Jornada the root of the problem was the explosion last month at Pemex's Cactus gas processing plant in the southern state of Chiapas.
Damaged units are still not on line at Cactus which has forced the shutdown of three ammonia plants in Cosoleacaque in the state of Veracruz.

Bonilla said the shutdowns have caused a artificial fertilizer shortage and caused increases in domestic prices of 25-45 percent in the last 20 days. Shortages have been noted in central and western states, it said.

Several national farm groups requested the temporary export suspension until domestic fertilizer markets, including urea and other ammonia-based products, calm down, Bonilla said. Pemex and ANIQ agreed to the proposal.

Mexican fertilizer prices, since the government ended the state monopoly of Fertilizantes Mexicanos (Fertimex), have not been controlled and are subject to market supply and demand. Distributors hike prices when shortages are noted.
